<pasted_content id="7015">
Task: add a small local check script for the live-mode model configuration. Create ONLY scripts/check-live-model.ts; do not edit any existing file (if a package.json script entry seems necessary, tell me instead of editing). Never read .env or print environment variables, keys or model output text. I will run the script myself; do not run it.
The script reads the same three environment variable names the deployment uses: LIVE_LLM_API_KEY, LIVE_LLM_BASE_URL, LIVE_LLM_MODEL (validate the model with the same pattern as src/server/live/config.ts; if any variable is missing or invalid, print only the variable NAMES and exit 1). It builds the real model client the same way realFactories in src/server/live/run-live.ts does (createGatewayLlmClient with the explicit key and base URL) and runs runImprovedPipeline on the FixtureProvider with the settings of the live path (LIVE_RUN_CONFIG with its model replaced by LIVE_LLM_MODEL; keep its 20-call cap and 1500 output tokens), with NO tracer, and writes NO files. It refuses to run unless the first command-line argument is exactly --confirm-spend (it makes real, small paid model calls). At the end it prints ONLY: the pipeline status; the number of prospects assessed, failed and not assessed; the failed-assessment reason codes with counts (codes only, never messages); the model_calls count; total input and output tokens if available; the llm_cost fields known_usd, complete and calls_by_basis; the model_basis, model_complete and model_calls_unavailable that modelCost in src/app/live/_lib/live-results.ts would produce for this run; and the elapsed seconds. It must never print prompts, model output text, company names, keys, the base URL or any error message from the provider (for a failed call print a fixed 'model call failed' plus the error class name only).
Read first: src/server/live/run-live.ts (realFactories, runLiveMode), src/server/live/config.ts, src/core/agent/improved-pipeline.ts and scripts/run-pipeline.ts (how the pipeline is invoked), src/core/data/fixture-provider.ts and src/app/live/_lib/live-results.ts. If importing modelCost from src/app is awkward from a script, replicate its small logic and say so. Run npx tsc --noEmit and npm run lint.
End with a plain-text SHORT REVIEW REPORT (under 20 lines, no code fences, no secrets): the file created, the exact command to run it (with environment variable NAMES only), the fixed output lines it prints, and anything you were unsure about.
</pasted_content id="7015">

content.text:
I've finished the work. Type check and lint both pass with no output, and I did not run the script.

SHORT REVIEW REPORT
File created: scripts/check-live-model.ts. It is the only change (git status shows just this untracked file). No package.json entry is needed.
Command: LIVE_LLM_API_KEY=... LIVE_LLM_BASE_URL=... LIVE_LLM_MODEL=... npx tsx scripts/check-live-model.ts --confirm-spend
Without --confirm-spend as the first argument it exits 2 and makes no calls. If a variable is missing or the model name fails the config.ts pattern, it prints "Missing or invalid: " followed by the variable names and exits 1.
Fixed output lines:
- status: ...
- prospects: assessed=.. failed=.. not_assessed=..
- failed_reasons: code=count,... (or none)
- model_calls: N
- tokens: input=.. output=..
- llm_cost: known_usd=.. complete=.. calls_by_basis=gateway_reported:..,estimated:..,unavailable:..
- model_cost: model_basis=.. model_complete=.. model_calls_unavailable=..
- elapsed_seconds: N.N
A failed call prints "model call failed (X)" while it runs.
The pipeline runs on FixtureProvider with the explicit key and base URL, LIVE_RUN_CONFIG with the model replaced, and no tracer. It writes no files.
modelCost is imported directly from src/app/live/_lib/live-results.ts, so nothing is replicated.
Unsure about:
- The model client returns errors instead of throwing, so there is no error class to print for most failures. In that case X is the fixed error category (for example rate_limited), not provider text. For a thrown error X is the class name.
- The script exits 1 if the pipeline status is "stopped", which you didn't ask for.
- It imports LIVE_RUN_CONFIG from run-live.ts, which also loads the synthetic-run module. That passed the type check, but I haven't confirmed it loads cleanly under tsx.
